chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: The airplane ticket that never came: quitting Eckstine
summary: Starving on $100 a week, he is left without a ticket to the Chicago engagement and decides he cannot gamble further.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And that was the last engagement that I played with Billy, because by this time, the money had really not gotten any better. I was still making this $100 a week, and I was really, literally starving to death! Anyway, the promising thing was supposed to have been an engagement in Chicago that

we were supposed to have that was supposed to pay me more money. Well, had a week off. So I came home. And the day that he was supposed to send me a plane ticket, and I was supposed to take the plane from Washington and meet him in Chicago... So when the date came a few days or a week or so later, when we were supposed to play there, I had heard nothing from Billy Eckstine.

So finally, I think the day before the engagement, I called Billy's house... And then he was married to June Eckstine. And I asked her for Billy. She said, "Hi, John. Billy's in Chicago." I said, "What?" She said, "Yeah. He left yesterday" or something. So I said, "I don't know what happened. He was supposed to send me a ticket." Anyway, I was very disappointed.

A week later, Billy called me to tell me about an engagement that we had in Seattle, I believe it was, and everything was going to be great. He mentioned something about the fact that when the thing happened in Chicago... He had some sort of a long story that he told me, which didn't sound like anything to me, because I think even if that did happen, he should have called me and told me about it. Nevertheless, I told him that I just didn't care to go that far speculating on making money, when I couldn't make it right here on the East Coast. So I regretfully just quit the job.
As a matter of fact, I had no choice.
